name: Web Plura Revenue Shield – Failed Payments & Revenue Recovery
author: Web Plura

sections.description:
Web Plura Revenue Shield helps WooCommerce stores review revenue-loss risks such as failed payments, pending orders, abandoned checkout signals, refund pressure, coupon issues, payment gateway patterns, stock problems, margin signals, and manual recovery opportunities.

The free WordPress.org plugin runs local revenue-risk scans inside WordPress. Store administrators can review the evidence behind each finding, export summaries, and organize follow-up work without sending store data to an external service for the included local features.

Revenue Shield is a review and recovery-assistance tool. It does not automatically contact customers, send abandoned-cart emails or SMS messages, process payments, issue refunds, or guarantee recovered revenue.

Key Revenue Risk Checks

Use Revenue Shield to review supported local signals such as:

  • failed and pending-payment orders;
  • abandoned checkout signals and manual recovery candidates;
  • refund and coupon pressure;
  • payment gateway, shipping, and checkout patterns;
  • low-stock, out-of-stock, dead-stock, and inventory-value indicators;
  • margin and profit estimates when cost data is available;
  • local recovery notes, review status, and recovered-value details;
  • CSV exports, JSON support exports, and print-ready summaries.

Failed and Pending Payments

Failed and pending-payment orders can quietly create support work, stock confusion, and missed follow-up. Revenue Shield reviews local WooCommerce order data so administrators can spot failed payments, pending-payment orders, on-hold orders, gateway patterns, and order records that may need manual review.

The plugin helps surface patterns for investigation. It does not fix payment gateways, retry payments, capture payment, or determine the root cause of every failed transaction.

Abandoned Checkout Signals

Revenue Shield can capture and summarize supported WooCommerce checkout signals after local processing consent is accepted. Where supported, checkout records use reduced or pseudonymous identifiers such as hashes instead of exposing unnecessary customer details in the recovery workflow.

These signals are for manual review. The free plugin does not send abandoned-cart emails, SMS reminders, coupons, or automated recovery sequences.

Refund and Coupon Risks

Refunds and coupon usage can point to product, shipping, pricing, support, or checkout problems. Revenue Shield reviews supported WooCommerce refund and coupon signals so store operators can compare patterns before deciding what needs attention.

These checks are operational indicators. They are not accounting reports, fraud determinations, or proof that a coupon or refund was improper.

Payment Gateway and Shipping Signals

Revenue Shield summarizes supported payment gateway and shipping-related signals from local WooCommerce order data. This can help administrators see whether failed or pending payments are concentrated around particular gateway patterns, or whether shipping estimates may deserve review.

The plugin does not monitor every gateway in real time and does not replace payment-provider diagnostics.

Margin and Profit Signals

When WooCommerce order or product cost data is available, Revenue Shield can show margin and profit-related estimates. These estimates are intended to help store operators notice low-margin signals and review revenue risk.

Margin and profit values depend on available cost data and should be treated as operational indicators, not formal accounting results.

Inventory and Stock Risks

Revenue Shield can review supported WooCommerce inventory signals such as low stock, out-of-stock products, stock value estimates, and dead-stock candidates.

These checks help connect inventory conditions with revenue risk. Revenue Shield does not replace WooCommerce inventory management and does not change product stock levels.

Recovery Opportunities

Revenue Shield turns selected failed, pending, stale, expired, cancelled, or checkout-review signals into local recovery opportunities. Administrators can inspect supporting evidence, save local notes, update review status, and record recovered-value details where supported.

The workflow is manual. Revenue Shield does not contact customers, send recovery messages, retry payments, or promise that flagged value can be recovered.

Reports and Exports

After a scan, administrators can review local reports, evidence summaries, issue/recommendation context, and recovery candidates in wp-admin.

Supported export workflows include CSV files, JSON support exports, print-ready summaries, and short handoff notes for store owners or support teams. Exports are designed around summaries and review context rather than raw customer-data dumps.

Local Processing and Privacy

The free plugin performs included WooCommerce scans, reports, exports, notes, and Recovery Opportunity review inside WordPress. A Web Plura account is not required for included local features.

Revenue Shield stores plugin-owned settings, scan summaries, consent state, abandoned-checkout records, recovery candidates, local notes, recovered-value details, and retention state in the site’s WordPress database. The plugin includes retention controls and WordPress privacy exporter/eraser support where plugin-owned personal data applies.

Uninstall removes plugin-owned options, scheduled cleanup hooks, and plugin-owned custom database tables.

Free Local Features and Optional Services

The WordPress.org plugin is focused on local WooCommerce review. Free local scans, reports, exports, platform cards, recovery candidates, notes, and privacy-safe controls remain useful without Web Plura Cloud, a subscription, a license, entitlement checks, checkout, or hosted services.

Optional hosted Web Plura services may provide additional workflows such as hosted report history, scheduled monitoring, additional commerce-source coverage, team reporting, or cloud-backed recovery workflow support. Those services are separate from the included local Free plugin behavior and should be checked on the official product page for current availability.

The Free plugin does not include Easy Digital Downloads or SureCart source support.

Important Limitations

Revenue Shield identifies supported local risk signals and review candidates. It cannot guarantee that every revenue issue is found, every checkout problem is diagnosed, or any flagged value can be recovered.

The Revenue Shield score summarizes supported local indicators detected by the plugin. It is an operational aid, not an accounting, fraud, tax, legal, or financial-health rating.

Store owners should review WooCommerce order notes, payment-provider information, fulfillment context, customer communication permissions, and store policy before taking follow-up action.

External Services

The free WordPress.org plugin does not connect to external services for its included local WooCommerce scans, reports, exports, local notes, or Recovery Opportunity review.

Optional hosted Web Plura Revenue Shield services are separate from the free plugin’s local operation. If an administrator chooses to use an optional hosted service, review the service documentation, terms, privacy policy, and consent controls before sending store data.

sections.installation:
1. Install the plugin from the WordPress.org plugin directory, or upload the web-plura-revenue-shield folder to /wp-content/plugins/.
  2. Make sure WooCommerce is installed and active if you want revenue-risk scans.
  3. Activate Revenue Shield from the Plugins screen.
  4. Open Revenue Shield in wp-admin.
  5. Review and accept processing consent.
  6. Run the first revenue-risk scan.
sections.faq:
What does Revenue Shield check?

Revenue Shield reviews supported WooCommerce revenue-risk signals including failed payments, pending orders, abandoned checkout signals, refunds, coupons, payment gateway patterns, shipping indicators, inventory, margin estimates, recovery candidates, and local report evidence.

Does Revenue Shield require setup before scans?

WooCommerce must be installed and active for Free local scans. Administrators also need to accept local processing consent before scans and local checkout-signal review run.

Can it help with WooCommerce failed payments?

Yes. The plugin reviews supported local WooCommerce failed-payment signals and can help administrators find orders, gateway patterns, and recovery candidates that may need investigation.

Can it find pending payment orders?

Yes. Revenue Shield reviews supported pending-payment and on-hold order signals so store operators can identify records that may need manual review.

Does it identify abandoned carts?

It identifies supported abandoned checkout signals and recovery candidates. It is not a complete abandoned-cart email platform and does not automatically contact shoppers.

Does Revenue Shield automatically contact customers?

No. The free plugin does not send emails, SMS messages, coupons, reminders, or automated recovery sequences.

Does it automatically recover payments?

No. Revenue Shield does not process payments, retry payments, issue refunds, or guarantee recovered revenue.

How are recovery opportunities created?

The plugin turns selected local order and checkout signals into recovery candidates with supporting evidence, estimated value, status, and local workflow details where supported.

Can I add recovery notes or status?

Yes. Administrators can update local review status, save notes, and record recovered-value details for supported recovery candidates.

Can it review refunds and coupon usage?

Yes. Revenue Shield reviews supported refund and coupon signals from WooCommerce order data so administrators can investigate patterns.

Does it analyze stock and inventory risks?

Yes. The plugin can review supported low-stock, out-of-stock, stock-value, and dead-stock indicators. It does not replace WooCommerce inventory management.

How are margin or profit estimates calculated?

Revenue Shield uses available WooCommerce order, product, or order-item cost data where present. Estimates depend on the data available on the site and should not be treated as formal accounting results.

Does Revenue Shield send store data to Web Plura Cloud?

The free WordPress.org plugin does not send included local scan, report, export, note, or recovery-review data to Web Plura Cloud. Optional hosted services are separate and require administrator choice and consent.

Is a Web Plura Cloud account required?

No. Included local WooCommerce scans, reports, exports, recovery candidates, notes, and privacy controls work without a Web Plura Cloud account.

What information is stored locally?

Depending on settings and site activity, Revenue Shield may store plugin-owned settings, consent state, scan summaries, abandoned-checkout records, recovery candidates, workflow status, notes, recovered-value details, retention state, and export/report state in WordPress.

Does it work without WooCommerce?

The free plugin is built for WooCommerce. If WooCommerce is not active, Revenue Shield shows dependency guidance instead of running local revenue-risk scans.

Can I export reports?

Yes. Supported exports include CSV files, JSON support exports, print-ready summaries, and handoff notes based on selected scan evidence.

What happens on uninstall?

Uninstall removes plugin-owned options, scheduled cleanup hooks, and plugin-owned custom database tables.
